title: Reduced-Carb Haloumi Shakshuka
subtitle: with Dukkah and Parsley
description: Can we have a ‘yay’ from the crowd for filling proteins, seasonal veggies and good, healthy fats? Our reduced-carb recipes feature all that, and contain less than 30 grams of carbohydrates per serve!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Thinly slice the capsicum and onion. Coarsely chop the parsley leaves, discarding the stems. Crush or finely chop the garlic. Slice the haloumi.

Cook haloumi: Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the haloumi for 2 mins each side or until golden. Remove from the pan. Heat 2 tsp olive oil in the pan over medium heat. Cook the capsicum and onion, stirring occasionally, for 7-8 mins until softened.

Simmer sauce: Add the garlic and Moroccan seasoning to the veggies and cook, stirring, for 30 secs or until fragrant. Stir in the tomato puree, half the tomato paste, 1 tsp honey and 80ml (⅓ cup) water and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 2 mins or until the capsicum is soft and the sauce is slightly reduced.

Add haloumi and eggs: Stir the haloumi into the sauce. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Using a spoon, make 2 shallow indents in the sauce. Carefully crack an egg into each indent. Cover and cook for 3-5 mins until the eggs are just cooked or cooked to your liking. Remove from the heat.
Serve up: Divide the shakshuka among bowls and scatter with the parsley and dukkah. Or, put the pan on the table for everyone to help themselves. Enjoy!

Did you know?: Haloumi is a brined, slightly springy cheese originally from Cyprus. Traditionally it was made from a mixture of goat and sheep milk, although these days cow's milk is also used. The haloumi we use is made using vegetable rennet, so it's suitable for vegetarians.
